item.title: Reps to probe rising human trafficking, trafficking networks
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the rising incidence of human trafficking in Nigeria, mandating its Committees on Human Rights, Interior and Police Affairs to probe the activities of trafficking syndicates and assess the effectiveness of existing measures to combat the crime. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Rep. Dominic Okafor, titled, “Need to Investigate the Alarming Increase in Human Trafficking in Nigeria”, at Wednesday’s plenary. The lawmakers expressed concern over the growing threat posed by human trafficking, particularly to women, children and other vulnerable groups. The House noted that human trafficking remained a grave violation of human rights and dignity, involving the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring or receipt of persons through force, coercion, deception, abuse of vulnerability or other prohibited means for the purpose of exploitation. It observed that victims were increasingly subjected to commercial sexual exploitation, forced labour, domestic servitude, forced begging, organ harvesting and other forms of degrading abuse. The lawmakers attributed the growing vulnerability of Nigerians to trafficking to poverty, unemployment, insecurity, displacement, irregular migration and the activities of organised criminal networks. They further noted that many victims were lured through false promises of employment, education, marriage and opportunities abroad, only to end up in exploitative conditions characterised by physical abuse, psychological trauma and, in some cases, death. The House also expressed concern that trafficking networks operated across state and international borders, exploiting porous borders, inadequate public awareness, weak coordination among relevant agencies and difficulties in identifying and prosecuting offenders. item.title: Zamfara: Jaji wins APC rerun primary by 26,646 votes
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau A member representing Kaura-Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) fresh primary election for the constituency with a landslide victory. Jaji emerged winner of the rerun primary conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, polling 26,646 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, who scored 713 votes. The third aspirant, Musa Zubairu, polled no votes. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the Kaura-Namoda/Birnin Magaji fresh primary, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the constituency’s collation centre in Kaura-Namoda. Giving a breakdown of the exercise, Idris said the constituency had 42,266 registered party members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited to vote, while 27,359 votes were cast. In the results announced, Jaji scored 14,264 votes in Kaura-Namoda Local Government Area, against Dangaladima’s 465 votes, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji Local Government Area, Jaji polled 12,382 votes, while Dangaladima secured 248 votes. Zubairu again scored zero. Declaring the result, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC constitution and the party’s guidelines, and was therefore returned as the winner of the fresh primary. The rerun followed a suit filed by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court, Abuja, which nullified Jaji’s earlier nomination and ordered the party to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The APC national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the rerun, in compliance with the court’s order. item.title: APC chieftain to DSS: Scrutinise Dino Melaye’s statements
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi An All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftain and loyalist of President Bola Tinubu, Khamis Musa Darazo, has urged the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to scrutinise recent statements attributed to former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, concerning the 2027 general elections. Darazo, who made the call while speaking with journalists in Bauchi on Thursday, said the move was necessary to safeguard national security and prevent political utterances capable of heightening tension or creating unnecessary apprehension among Nigerians. He, however, cautioned that his call should not be interpreted as an attempt to intimidate opposition politicians or suppress democratic freedoms, stressing that democracy accommodates criticism, disagreement and healthy political competition. According to him, political leaders must recognise the responsibility that comes with public statements, particularly as the country approaches another election cycle. “This is not about persecution, intimidation or silencing the opposition. It is about responsibility. If a statement made by a prominent political actor has generated legitimate security concerns, the authorities have every right to seek clarification and establish the facts,” he said. Darazo maintained that security agencies must apply the law fairly, irrespective of political affiliation, warning against the use of national security as a partisan instrument. He also urged Melaye and other political leaders to exercise restraint in their public statements, saying Nigeria could not afford another atmosphere of political tension, fear and confrontation ahead of the 2027 elections. “Political disagreement is normal in a democracy. What is unacceptable is allowing political competition to gradually become a source of tension among citizens. We should sell our ideas, present our records and persuade Nigerians rather than create unnecessary anxiety,” he added. item.title: 2027: SDP inaugurates 12,000-member campaign council, names Tanko coordinator
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) has inaugurated a 12,000-member Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, with Dr Yunusa Tanko appointed as its National Coordinator. The SDP National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, who will also serve as chairman of the council, inaugurated the campaign council on Wednesday in Abuja. Gombe charged members of the council to work towards securing electoral victory for the party, stressing that its campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and guided by the provisions of the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) guidelines and the party’s constitution. He urged members to approach the election with the seriousness it deserved, adding that the party was determined to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “Let us approach this election with the seriousness it deserves to unseat President Tinubu. “Our campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and firmly rooted in the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the Electoral Act, INEC guidelines and our party constitution. “We must earn the confidence of Nigerians through credible engagement, persuasion, effective organisation and practical policy alternatives. “We must reject violence, intimidation, electoral malpractice and every conduct capable of undermining the integrity of our democracy,” he said. The SDP chairman described Nigeria as being at a critical crossroads, citing insecurity, economic hardship, unemployment, poverty, institutional weaknesses and declining public confidence in governance as some of the challenges confronting the country. According to him, Nigerians are yearning for purposeful leadership, economic opportunities, social justice, security and accountability, as well as a government that prioritises their welfare and dignity. He said the SDP was determined to provide Nigerians with a credible democratic alternative founded on social justice, equity, freedom, inclusive development and good governance. Gombe urged members of the campaign council to take the party’s message to communities across the country, engage citizens respectfully, listen to their concerns and demonstrate through their conduct that the party deserved their confidence. He further charged the council to ensure that the party’s campaign remained peaceful, credible and focused on offering practical solutions to the country’s challenges. item.title: Obi prefers ‘anywhere food is ready politics’ – Wike
item.description: Says, Atiku won’t get 25% across South By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Mr Peter Obi, prefers “anywhere food is ready politics”. Wike spoke on Tuesday when he met youth stakeholders in the FCT to campaign for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election. “Obi is not going anywhere. Don’t deceive yourself. If he likes, let him enter the motorcycle and carry everybody at the back; he is not going anywhere,” the minister said. He mocked Obi’s visits to camps for internally displaced persons (IDPs). ” He goes to IDP camp to do birthdays. When he was governor, did he do that? No. Very soon, they will start going along the trees, buying and chewing corn. “He prefers anywhere Mama Put is ready for politics. He doesn’t want to struggle. Small fight, he ran away from the PDP. He did the same in the Labour Party, and now he is in NDC. But, as for me, I am not afraid of fighting. They have now run away from the PDP, and I am still in the party,” he said. The minister also dismissed the chances of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress ADC presidential candidate. “Atiku won’t get 25 per cent in South South, South East and South West. Where will he get it?” he asked. He urged the youths to do more than vote for Tinubu. “Please, I beg of you, not to just come out to vote, not to just endorse this president here, mobilise all your colleagues, even those who are not part of your association, reach out to them, and get everybody to come out. “I am not a member of the All Progressives Congress. You don’t need to be an APC member or a Peoples Democratic Party PDP member for you to contribute to the development of your country. All you need to do is to work according to the vision of the person who has appointed you. Let’s not put our destiny in the hands of political gamblers who have been gambling for over 22 years,” he said. Wike reminded the youths of the record of earlier administrations on their welfare and that of women in the FCT. “Atiku Abubakar was vice president from 1999 to 2007. Is it not correct? Correct. Was there any establishment of a youth secretariat? No. Was there any establishment of a women’s secretariat? No. From 1976 to 2023, nobody cared,” he added. He said Tinubu changed that within a year of taking office. “Go and make sure there is a youth secretary. Go and make sure there’s a woman secretary,” he quoted the president as directing. He urged the youths to ignore showmanship. “Leave all these rhetorics; leave all this drama. These are cosmetic. Let us face the reality on the ground. That is what matters,” he said. item.title: Kerrygold Engages Women in Business and Leadership at 25th WIMBIZ Annual Conference
item.description: Kerrygold, the renowned Irish dairy brand from Ornua, strengthened its engagement with consumers at the 25th Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) Annual Conference, held on November 5 and 6, 2026, at Eko Hotel & Suites, Lagos. The conference, which marked 25 years of WIMBIZ’s commitment to empowering women, brought together business leaders, entrepreneurs, professionals and public sector executives for conversations around leadership, enterprise development and the evolving role of women in business. This year’s edition was themed “Rooted, Rising, Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World.” As a sponsor of the conference, Kerrygold leveraged the platform to increase brand visibility, deepen consumer engagement and strengthen its relevance among an audience of accomplished and influential women. A key feature of its participation was an exhibition stand where attendees had the opportunity to discover the brand, learn more about its product offerings and sample its products. The activation provided an opportunity for direct interaction with consumers, allowing guests to experience Kerrygold firsthand while creating meaningful brand touchpoints beyond traditional brand visibility. Through these engagements, Kerrygold reinforced its commitment to bringing its quality dairy products closer to consumers and building lasting relationships through relevant experiences. Commenting on the brand’s participation, Titilayo Ijiyokunola, General Manager, Ornua Dairy Products Nigeria Ltd., said: “At Kerrygold, we recognise the important role women play in shaping businesses, industries and communities. Our participation at WIMBIZ provides an opportunity to connect with this community, recognise their contributions and support platforms that champion leadership, enterprise and professional growth.” Kerrygold’s participation at the conference reflects its continued interest in engaging consumers through platforms that bring people together, create opportunities for meaningful interactions and allow more people to experience the quality and distinctive offerings of the brand. Built on generations of dairy knowledge and heritage, Kerrygold is made with the finest milk from grass-fed cows and quality ingredients, with no artificial ingredients. In Nigeria, Kerrygold Milk is manufactured and distributed by Ornua Nigeria, bringing the brand’s distinctive rich, creamy taste and heritage to consumers across the country. item.title: Nigeria’s crude oil output drops to 1.51m bpd in October — NUPRC
item.description: Nigeria’s crude oil production declined slightly to 1.51 million barrels per day (bpd) in October 2026, from 1.53 million bpd recorded in September, according to data from the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC). The figure represents a 1.7 per cent month-on-month decline. Despite the drop, Nigeria maintained crude oil production above its Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) quota of 1.5 million bpd for the sixth consecutive month in 2026. OPEC data showed that Nigeria produced 1.5 million bpd in August, 1.50 million bpd in July, 1.55 million bpd in June and 1.53 million bpd in May. When condensates are included, the country’s average daily production stood at 1.68 million barrels in October. NUPRC data also showed that daily production peaked at 1.79 million barrels during the month, while the lowest output was 1.60 million barrels per day. The commission attributed the relatively stable production levels in recent months to improved operational stability, production uptime and crude evacuation efficiency. “The sustained growth recorded in October reflects the continued commitment of operators and industry stakeholders towards improving operational efficiency, maintaining asset integrity, and enhancing production reliability across the Nigerian upstream petroleum sector,” the commission said. A breakdown of daily average crude oil and condensate production by terminals and streams showed that Forcados recorded the highest output at 318,490 barrels per day, followed by Bonny Terminal with 311,020 bpd. Qua Iboe Terminal recorded an average production of 173,970 bpd, while Escravos Oil Terminal posted a daily average of 134,670 bpd. The commission added that Bonga ranked as the fifth-highest producing terminal, recording an average of 106,650 bpd of crude oil and condensate. item.title: Reps seek emergency funding for teaching hospitals as health budget falls to 4.2%
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to urgently increase funding for federal teaching hospitals, federal medical centres, the National Hospital Abuja and other tertiary health institutions, warning that inadequate resources are undermining specialist healthcare delivery across the country. The lawmakers also urged the government to establish a dedicated infrastructure revitalisation programme, improve the welfare of healthcare workers and ensure timely release of approved funds to the institutions. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Patrick Umoh during Wednesday’s plenary, in which he drew attention to declining health budget allocations, deteriorating infrastructure, inadequate medical equipment and the continued migration of doctors, nurses and other skilled professionals. Presenting the motion, Umoh said federal tertiary health institutions remained central to specialist medical services, healthcare training and research but were struggling with dilapidated facilities, insufficient bed spaces, unreliable electricity supply and rising operational costs. He said urgent legislative intervention was necessary to strengthen the institutions and ensure that Nigerians had access to quality, affordable and accessible specialist healthcare. The lawmaker also commended the Federal Government for its continued interest in and prioritisation of the health sector. However, he expressed concern that Nigeria’s health sector allocation remained significantly below the 15 per cent commitment made by African governments under the 2001 Abuja Declaration. According to the motion, the proposed federal health budget allocation declined from approximately 5.33 per cent in 2023 to 4.20 per cent in the proposed 2026 budget. Umoh also cited figures indicating that only 30 per cent of the health sector’s 2023 capital appropriation was released, while approximately 15.06 per cent of the 2024 capital allocation was reportedly released and utilised. The motion further stated that only N36 million was reportedly released from the N218 billion appropriated for the Ministry of Health’s 2025 capital expenditure. item.content:encoded: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to urgently increase funding for federal teaching hospitals, federal medical centres, the National Hospital Abuja and other tertiary health institutions, warning that inadequate resources are undermining specialist healthcare delivery across the country. The lawmakers also urged the government to establish a dedicated infrastructure revitalisation programme, improve the welfare of healthcare workers and ensure timely release of approved funds to the institutions. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Patrick Umoh during Wednesday’s plenary, in which he drew attention to declining health budget allocations, deteriorating infrastructure, inadequate medical equipment and the continued migration of doctors, nurses and other skilled professionals. Presenting the motion, Umoh said federal tertiary health institutions remained central to specialist medical services, healthcare training and research but were struggling with dilapidated facilities, insufficient bed spaces, unreliable electricity supply and rising operational costs. He said urgent legislative intervention was necessary to strengthen the institutions and ensure that Nigerians had access to quality, affordable and accessible specialist healthcare. The lawmaker also commended the Federal Government for its continued interest in and prioritisation of the health sector. However, he expressed concern that Nigeria’s health sector allocation remained significantly below the 15 per cent commitment made by African governments under the 2001 Abuja Declaration. According to the motion, the proposed federal health budget allocation declined from approximately 5.33 per cent in 2023 to 4.20 per cent in the proposed 2026 budget. Umoh also cited figures indicating that only 30 per cent of the health sector’s 2023 capital appropriation was released, while approximately 15.06 per cent of the 2024 capital allocation was reportedly released and utilised. The motion further stated that only N36 million was reportedly released from the N218 billion appropriated for the Ministry of Health’s 2025 capital expenditure. The lawmaker warned that inadequate funding had contributed to overcrowded hospitals, delays in treatment, poor maintenance of facilities and shortages of essential medical equipment, forcing some patients to seek treatment in private hospitals or abroad. He also linked the growing migration of doctors, consultants and nurses to the declining capacity of public tertiary hospitals to provide specialist services. Umoh said the recently reported Ebola case in Nigeria had further underscored the need to strengthen the country’s tertiary health institutions and their capacity to respond to public health emergencies. Consequently, the House urged the Federal Government to substantially increase allocations to federal teaching hospitals, medical centres, the National Hospital Abuja and other tertiary institutions in the 2027 Supplementary Appropriation Bill and subsequent budgets. It also called for a dedicated tertiary healthcare infrastructure revitalisation programme to rehabilitate existing facilities, expand hospital capacity and provide modern medical equipment. On manpower, the lawmakers urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare to conduct a comprehensive assessment of staffing needs across federal tertiary institutions and develop a properly funded recruitment and retention programme. They further called for improved welfare packages, specialist allowances, professional development opportunities and other incentives to discourage healthcare professionals from leaving public hospitals. The House also urged the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation to ensure the timely and adequate release of approved allocations, particularly capital and overhead funds. Other recommendations included dedicated funding for electricity, water supply, equipment maintenance, medical consumables and other essential operational needs of the institutions. He remains in post, but it is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. item.title: Soludo celebrates Anambra-born U-17 Golden Ball winner, Umejiaku
item.description: By Steve Oko Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has celebrated Oluebube Umejiaku, the Anambra-born midfielder who emerged the Most Valuable Player at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Umejiaku won the prestigious Golden Ball award after inspiring Nigeria’s Flamingos to a historic 2-1 victory over Japan in the final played on November 7. The talented midfielder also scored Nigeria’s decisive second goal, sealing the victory and earning the Player of the Match award in the final. The triumph marked the first time an African women’s national team had won a FIFA World Cup title at any level. Soludo, through his Chief Press Secretary, Christian Aburime, described Umejiaku’s performance at the tournament as superlative. In recognition of her achievement, the Chairman of the Anambra State Football Association, General Chikelue Iloenyosi, travelled to Abuja on November 9 to receive and celebrate the young football star on behalf of the state government. Iloenyosi commended Soludo for his commitment to sports development and efforts to identify and nurture sporting talents across the state. He said Umejiaku’s emergence on the global stage underscored the importance of grassroots sports development and sustained investment in young talents. The Golden Ball winner’s achievement has also been described as a major source of inspiration to aspiring female footballers in Anambra State and the South-East. From her early football development to becoming the standout player at a global tournament, Umejiaku’s rise represents a significant milestone for women’s football in the state. Her performance in Morocco has further highlighted Nigeria’s potential in women’s youth football and placed her among the emerging talents attracting attention on the global stage. Despite the operational gains, Disu acknowledged that bandit attacks were continuing in some parts of the country, with affected communities facing threats to their safety and livelihoods. He consequently directed Commissioners of Police in affected states to submit updated threat assessments and operational requirements to Force Headquarters within 72 hours. He also ordered the intensification of intelligence-led operations and directed every command to maintain a standing operational plan for high-risk areas. The IGP called for stronger community intelligence, urging police commands to engage traditional rulers, village heads, hunters’ associations and local vigilante groups in affected areas. item.title: VIDEO: Tinubu Receives Flamingos In Abuja After World Cup Victory
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has received the Flamingos after winning Africa’s first-ever U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, received the victorious players and technical crew on behalf of the President at the Presidential Banquet Hall, Abuja. ﻿ The U-17 team won their first FIFA World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. The Flamingos lost their opener 2-1 to Poland, but dominated in the remaining matches, defeating defending champions North Korea, Puerto Rico, and Mexico. Their first-ever appearance in the final was sealed with a 3-1 victory over Brazil, before taking home the trophy after beating Japan. Flamingos celebrating their U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup The players have received commendations from government officials and football fans around the world. President Tinubu congratulated the Flamingos for becoming the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, said he received the news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States. He also described Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the country and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. The Senate also pledged a ₦100 million reward for the Flamingos. The pledge followed a motion moved by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ningi, who congratulated the players on their outstanding performance and commended the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) for its role in the team’s achievement. The latest feat by a Nigerian sports team came less than two years after the senior women’s football team, Super Falcons, won their 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in Morocco. He said the suspects were neutralized and the following items were captured; two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines and over 5,000 rounds of ammunition. According to him, on November 4th, 2026, troops exploited into Obele Forest, neutralised three kidnappers and captured four AK-47 rifles, 12 magazines, 336 rounds of 7.62mm Special ammunition and three bandoliers.
